environment.notCovered: Tauri WebKitGTK runtime, physical pen pressure, non-Chromium engines

screenshots.inspection: Photo workspace, real rectangular marquee boundary on the canvas, Selection Sources inspector showing Refine selection -> Operation: Feather with its radius control. Marching ants are visible as a dashed rectangle.

After Feather then Grow: the operation select shows Grow, the Apply button and the 50%-contour explanation are present, and the dashed boundary is visibly larger than in the before capture, confirming the operation committed to coverage rather than only to the panel.
Design tab, MASK section expanded on the selected image before any mask exists: the button reads Create brush mask… and the image is fully visible.

After a deliberate three-step fast drag: only the painted horizontal band of the image remains visible and the rest shows the artboard; the MASK section now reads Paint mask… with TYPE: ALPHA and Remove. The continuous band proves pointer-sample interpolation filled the gaps of the coarse drag.
After one Ctrl+Z the full image is restored, confirming the mask stroke was one undoable document operation and the source image pixels were never modified.

notes: The spec asserts colored-pixel counts before/after/undo, so the visual claims are backed by numerical checks, not screenshots alone.

A real pointer bug was found during this validation: a stroke that began outside the target image aborted the whole gesture because the first mapped sample was null (fixed in RefineMaskTool and TrimapEditTool).
